Segment root is backend/servers/api-server/src/ excl. routes/ (the skill's segment-map path backend/api-server/src/handlers/ is stale for this repo layout; the real api-core surface is services/ ~20.7k LOC + the top-level client_ip/state/preflight/observability files). This is a mature, heavily-hardened segment and most patterns scanned came up CLEAN this pass (recorded so future rotations don't re-mine speculatively): (a) UNWRAP/EXPECT crash paths — essentially all non-test unwrap/expect are inside #[cfg(test)] mods (totp/jwt/voice_commands/scheduler) or infallible const-string parses (Decimal::from_str("0.5").unwrap, threshold weights); totp.rs:153 .expect("OS rng failed") is a documented fail-closed nonce invariant, not a defect. (b) CWE-209 raw-DB-error leak — the api-handlers class does NOT reproduce here: services wrap errors as AppError::Database(e.to_string()) but the accounting/matches route maps AppError -> bare StatusCode (full error logged server-side, only a status returned to the client), and there is no blanket `impl IntoResponse for AppError` that would serialize self.to_string() into a response body. (c) SSRF — actions/api_call.rs is exemplary: connect-time SsrfGuardResolver, redirect-hop validation via common::url_validation, same-origin credential-header stripping. (d) Stripe webhook verify_signature uses constant-time ct_eq, an overflow-proof timestamp-skew helper, and fails closed. (e) Outbound email HTML (email.rs) consistently html_escape()s / ammonia::clean()s user-controlled fields. The two findings below are the genuine net-new defects: a mislabelled .expect() over env-overridable Argon2 params that can panic the server at boot, and a batch-abort error-propagation asymmetry in the workflow trigger loop. Neither has an existing backlog finding (grep of backlog.json for argon2/auth-service/workflow-condition returned nothing).

evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/auth.rs:49-62 — AuthService::new() reads three Argon2id cost parameters from the environment (PPT_ARGON2_M_COST_KIB, PPT_ARGON2_T_COST, PPT_ARGON2_P_COST), each via `std::env::var(..).ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(<default>)`, then builds `Params::new(m_cost, t_cost, p_cost, None).expect("argon2 params hard-coded above the library minimum, cannot fail")`. The .expect() message is factually wrong: three of the four inputs are operator-supplied env values, NOT hard-coded. argon2::Params::new validates its arguments and returns Err for out-of-range combinations (e.g. t_cost == 0, p_cost == 0, or m_cost < 8*p_cost). A single malformed-but-parseable env value — e.g. PPT_ARGON2_T_COST=0 (parses fine as u32, then rejected by Params::new) — makes .expect() panic.

Reachability: AuthService::new() is invoked while constructing AppState at api-server startup, so a bad env value does not degrade gracefully — it panics the whole server on boot (an operator-misconfiguration DoS). Note the asymmetry with the sibling cost reads, which already tolerate a *garbage* value by falling back to the default via `.parse().ok()`; a *parseable-but-out-of-range* value defeats that same intent and crashes instead. The reassuring .expect() comment actively discourages a future reader from adding the missing bound check.

Net-new: grep of .research/backlog.json for argon2 / auth-service / params-new returned no existing finding. Landable backend-only remedy (confined to auth.rs): either clamp each env value to the Argon2 valid range before Params::new, or match on the Params::new Err and `tracing::warn!` + fall back to the documented defaults (m=65536,t=3,p=1) instead of .expect(). Verifiable via `cargo build -p api-server` + a unit test that sets PPT_ARGON2_T_COST=0 and asserts AuthService::new() returns a working hasher rather than panicking. Confidence medium: the panic is confirmed by static read of the Params::new contract; exact production env values are deployment-dependent, so reachability is operator-triggered rather than user-triggered.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs — trigger_workflows_for_event loads every workflow subscribed to an event and iterates them. Inside the loop (around :359) it evaluates each workflow's stored conditions with `if !self.evaluate_conditions(&conditions, &context)? { continue; }`. The `?` propagates a WorkflowError (evaluate_conditions returns Err(WorkflowError::ConditionError) at :523 when a workflow's stored condition JSON parses as neither a ConditionGroup nor a Condition) out of the ENTIRE batch function, aborting processing of every remaining subscribed workflow for that event.

This is an error-handling asymmetry: the actual workflow execution a few lines down (:392-403) deliberately catches a per-workflow Err and `tracing::warn!`s + continues, so one failing execution never blocks the others — but the condition-evaluation step does the opposite and lets one tenant's malformed-condition workflow suppress all other legitimate workflows triggered by the same event. The conditions come from persisted `workflow.conditions.0`, so a single bad config written at any time silently degrades automation for unrelated workflows on every matching event thereafter.

Net-new: grep of .research/backlog.json for workflow-condition / evaluate-conditions / aborts-batch returned no existing finding. Landable backend-only remedy (confined to workflow_executor.rs): treat a ConditionError like the execute_workflow Err arm — log it against the offending workflow_id and `continue` to the next workflow instead of `?`-propagating, so a malformed condition is isolated to its own workflow. Verifiable via `cargo build -p api-server` + a unit test with two workflows on one event where the first has a malformed condition JSON, asserting the second still runs. Confidence medium: the propagation path is confirmed by static read; whether a malformed stored condition exists in production is data-dependent, so the trigger is latent rather than runtime-confirmed.
